title: C6 continuity state (bbolt)
description: What the core keeps durably so that a restarted core can reattach (Storage §8.6: anything the core must know to request the right byte range from a surviving worker is durable; everything else is derived; immortality §7, §9: bbolt, never Redis). U5 defines the buckets and U2 writes them (plan.md §3 C6). One JSON value per key: the sessions bucket holds a session_record per session id, the connections bucket a connection_record per connection id, and the grid_snapshots bucket a grid_snapshot_record per session id. The session record is the layout the E0 core already writes, so an E0 record loads unchanged — the migration-free rule plan.md §3 sets for C6 — plus optional fields. Storage §8.6's durable list maps onto it: session_id and target are in the nested northbound record, the owner is the principal in session.owner (locally the owner token is authority held by a principal, not a bearer secret, so there is no opaque owner-token id: an id nothing reads is dead state), protocol, last_committed_seq is recording_last_seq_out, which the core realigns to the recording's end before every C3 hello (below), recording_path, and the timers' two clocks. From contract-v0.3 the record also carries stale_seq and stale_cause, so a pending stale-grid choice survives a second restart (5.52): after a declared gap, or a grid that could not be rebuilt though no byte was lost, the core persists where staleness began and why, in the same bbolt write as the gap commit and the forced grid snapshot (grid_snapshots); cleared on the answer. One persisted value, not two: the commit point — recording_last_seq_out, recording_committed_offset, out_bytes_committed and recording_last_seq_in, four numbers for one point of the recording — advances only when a grid_snapshot_record is persisted, in the same bbolt write, so at every write snapshot_seq equals recording_last_seq_out, which is immortality §4.1's last_committed_seq (5.39). A session with no grid_snapshot_record — a session type that gets no grid, or a shell before its first snapshot or after its snapshot was refused — has no snapshot_seq to align with: its commit point moves in a record-only write wherever a snapshot would be stored and none can be. Except for a quarantined predecessor, which stays at P and continues in a linked successor (terminal-output-accounting §5.3), before every C3 hello the core realigns: it moves the commit point to the recording's end, with a snapshot of a grid that has applied every output frame the recording holds (at a core restart, the snapshot restored and the recording's own output frames past the commit point re-fed), or with a record-only write for a session with no snapshot. So hello's last_committed_seq is snapshot_seq, the worker replays only seq > snapshot_seq, which is exactly what the recording lacks (immortality §4.1, §5.1), and a gap is declared only for output that neither the recording nor the ring holds (immortality §4.3). The wait for that snapshot is bounded by the knob snapshot.wait_sec (grid-snapshot rule 12). When it runs out, or the VT worker cannot give the snapshot, the core gives the grid up rather than hold the recording: it deletes the grid_snapshot_record, realigns record-only, sends hello, and raises the stale flow with cause grid_lost. The recording ranks above the grid: "the byte stream is byte-perfect" while "grid continuity is best-effort" (open_decisions §4), and "core downtime = recording gap = audit hole = contract violation" (immortality §4). A session whose end the core already knows realigns record-only, its snapshot deleted, since its grid is never shown again. The recording is never cut back: no byte that reached the broker is dropped from it (open_decisions §5, LOCKED; Contract §13). On a restart the core cuts only a torn last frame of a non-quarantined pair and finds that recording's end by walking it forward from the commit point (ttyrec.schema.json x-sidecar reopen). A gap marker a handshake writes is a commit point: the write that commits it — the gap's forced snapshot, in the stale_seq write above, or a record-only write for a session with no snapshot or after snapshot.wait_sec — lands before the core appends any later frame but an end marker. For a session that is not recorded, the recording's end means the last output frame the core has received, and after a restart what the grid it restores or keeps has applied; nothing re-feeds its grid, so a VT worker's death loses that grid (stale flow, cause grid_lost). Restore is the snapshot, then the recording's own output frames past it, then the worker's replay. Cost, stated plainly: a reattach first rebuilds and snapshots each grid the recording has outrun, waiting at most snapshot.wait_sec, after which that grid is lost; a graceful stop snapshots every such grid first, so an ordinary restart pays nothing; a restart reads each recording from its commit point, which the snapshot cadence keeps near its end. What is not here, on purpose: no claim token (immortality §6.1, LOCKED: a local reattach is SO_PEERCRED alone; decision 5.30); no control-token escrow state — Storage §8.6 keeps the control-token holder in memory, and immortality §7 escrows the token on every restart, so the nested record's control_holder is its northbound shape, reads null after any restart, and a core never restores a holder from it. unreachable_reason lives only in the nested record: one copy, not two. orphan-pending has no durable writer — the core is gone while it holds — and its outcome arrives as killed / orphan through the spool (spool-entry.schema.json).

session_record.description: sessions bucket: session id → this record.

session.description: The northbound record (C1), state and unreachable_reason included. Its control_holder is null after any restart: the control token goes to escrow (immortality §7). The core keeps the record's resizable for the session's life, so a restarted core reads back the value the worker reported on channel_opened, and never changes it.

owner_id.description: Reserved for RBAC tenancy (Storage §9: on every record from day one, so wiring it later needs no migration); "" until then. The owner itself is session.owner.

tenant_id.description: Reserved as owner_id is; "" until RBAC tenancy is wired.

recording_path.description: The session's .ttyrec (C8): audit data (Storage §6), never northbound (Contract §4). Absent when the session is not recorded.

recording_active_path.description: The active continuation ttyrec; absent means recording_path. Offsets are local to this pair; terminal-output-accounting.md.

recording_next_generation.description: Next continuation generation; absent means 1. Reserve durably before pair creation and never reuse a generation. An exclusive-create collision after bbolt restoration halts and is reported.

input_seq_reserved_through.description: For recorded sessions only: the durably reserved input sequence high-water; reserve before assigning above it. For an unrecorded session recording_last_seq_in itself holds its reservation high-water; the two representations are mutually exclusive, never competing floors. On continuation from a quarantined pair the active switch uses this as the empty pair's input base.

recording_held.description: Persisted per-session recording hold: set by the quarantine-hold write; clear in the live active-switch write, or after an ended held session's successor end marker is synced. The in-process hold applies first.

recording_end_placement.description: Pair-specific end-placement proofs persist across active-pair switches; paths are unique.

recording_committed_offset.description: Pair-local offset in the active .ttyrec; counts are session-wide across trusted predecessors and the active pair. The commit point's place in the .ttyrec: the end of a frame, after output frame (or gap marker) recording_last_seq_out and before the next output frame or gap marker; out_bytes_committed and recording_last_seq_in count the frames before it. The core makes both recording files durable through it before the write that stores it, so a restart's walk starts at a frame both files hold (ttyrec.schema.json x-sidecar reopen).

recording_last_seq_out.description: Session-wide across the trusted chain, including a successor: immortality §4.1's last_committed_seq: the seq of the last output frame or gap marker at the commit point — a gap marker counts as the seq of the gap frame it records, the last lost seq. It equals snapshot_seq (decision 5.39: one counter, aligned) and moves only in the write that stores a grid snapshot, or in a record-only write for a session with no grid_snapshot_record; before an ordinary hello the core moves it to the unquarantined recording's end; a held or quarantined pair stays at P until active switch, so it is the value hello carries (continuity-state top). A gap marker a handshake writes is a commit point: its write lands before any later frame is appended, so a core that dies after it asks for what follows the loss, and no loss is declared twice. One counter, not a renamed copy beside it — a second field meaning the same seq would be two counters that can drift.

recording_last_seq_in.description: The session-wide input base or seq of the last input frame before the active pair-local recording_committed_offset, written with the commit point. The core's own counter: at a continuation switch the empty pair inherits the durable reservation as its input base; after a normal restart it continues from this seq plus the input frames the recording keeps past that offset (ttyrec.schema.json x-sidecar reopen), so no input seq is used twice. A session that is not recorded keeps no input frame to count: the core continues it from a floor no earlier seq can reach — at E2 a reservation it writes ahead of the input seqs it uses; an E1 core's floor conforms.

client_touch_at.description: unattended's clock: the last byte a client sent (session model §10 client_touch), from session creation. Durable, so a core restart does not restart the timer (session model §15; phase-01). Read with a numeric offset from a record an earlier core wrote in its local zone; written in UTC with Z.

activity_at.description: idle's clock: the last byte either way (session model §10 activity), from session creation. Durable, like client_touch_at, and read and written the same way. The recording continuation's active-switch write sets it to the switch time, so idle re-arms from the switch after a crash (terminal-output-accounting §5.3; session-countdown).

end_reason.description: Why the session ended, persisted with its state the first time the end is known and held unchanged after (session model §12). Absent while it lives.

ended_at.description: When it ended, as seen by the component that observed the end — the worker's stamp for a spooled end. Absent while it lives.

protocol.description: The connect protocol of its connection (Storage §8.6). Optional: an E0 record lacks it. Later tags add values.

out_bytes_committed.description: The session-wide output payload bytes across trusted predecessors and the active pair through the frame or gap marker recording_last_seq_out names, declared losses included: the code-0 payload the recording keeps before recording_committed_offset plus the byte counts of its code-2 gap markers there. It describes exactly the point recording_last_seq_out describes, is persisted in the same write, and is written on every session record a v0.2 core holds — for a session born at E0, computed from its recording at the first E1 start. A gap marker's byte count is first_buffered_offset (or the spool's out_bytes) minus the output bytes the recording holds — this count, plus a gap marker the recording holds past the commit point (ttyrec.schema.json x-sidecar reopen) — so a count that drifted would state a false loss, which is what immortality §4.3 exists to prevent. Optional only because E0 records lack it.

stale_seq.description: Where the session's staleness began, present exactly when a stale-choice is pending — for both causes. For cause gap it is the gap frame's seq; for cause grid_lost it is the committed seq at which the grid could not be rebuilt. This carries, durably, where staleness began for both causes; the wire's gap_seq is the only seq on the C2 stale frame, and it exists only for cause gap. Written in the same bbolt write as the gap commit and the forced grid snapshot (a crash between committing the gap marker and persisting stale_seq is covered); a grid_lost is found at restore, before any new commit, so its write stands alone and precedes the first new commit, or rides the record-only commit that gives the grid up (grid-snapshot rule 12). Cleared when the choice is answered. Optional: absent when no choice is pending, and on a v0.2 record.

stale_cause.description: Why the session is stale, present exactly when stale_seq is. gap: a declared loss of target output. grid_lost: a grid that cannot be rebuilt with no byte lost (snapshot_incompatible or seq_jump). Both-or-neither with stale_seq, as the ends_at / ends_by / ending trio is written; a receiver that meets a value it does not know shows the stale notice without a cause.

connection_record.description: connections bucket: connection id → this record — the local worker and session metadata a restarted core needs to request replay (development-plan §2 v0.2).

credential_ref.description: Which credential the connection authenticated with: target × credential decides what may share a connection (Contract §15.3). A reference, never the credential. From proto_version 0.5, a telnet connection authenticates with nothing, so on a telnet connection_record this names the credential that authorized the create, not one used for authentication. From the vault release it is a vault reference (common.schema.json#/$defs/credential_ref), told apart by credential_layer, since a personal and an org credential may share a name; or the constant supplied for a connection opened with a supplied login or a device login, which `login` tells apart.

credential_layer.description: From the vault release: the layer of credential_ref, so target × credential (reference and layer) decides what may share a connection (Contract §15.3). Absent on a record an earlier core wrote, and for a supplied or a prompted login.

login.description: From Release B (OPEN-R2 (a)): where the connection's login came from, the value session.connect's detail.login takes for it: `stored` (a credential the core resolved), `supplied` (the login a create request carried) or `prompted` (a device login, answers typed at the device's own prompts). credential_ref stays the constant `supplied` for the last two, so `login` is what tells them apart: it lets a prompted connection stay reusable by its principal, by connection_id, across a restart, and a rebuilt session.connect says prompted. Placement: `supplied` and `prompted` only beside credential_ref `supplied`; `stored` only beside another reference; the schema refuses a record that puts one out of place. A core of this release writes it on every SSH connection record it makes (stored, supplied or prompted) and never on a telnet or echo one. An absent value reads as credential_ref says (supplied for the constant, otherwise stored on an SSH connection), so every record an earlier core wrote keeps its meaning; an earlier core reads a record that carries it by ignoring the field.

proto_version.description: The worker's C3 version; absent for a v0.1 worker, whose connection is never a reuse candidate.

session_ids.description: The sessions on it that have not been released.

buffer_bytes.description: The value this connection was connected with, fixed for its life (ipc-control.schema.json connect). Absent for a v0.1 worker's connection, which had none.

input_frame_max.description: The value this connection was connected with, fixed for its life: a restarted core splits client input at this, never at a value its configuration now holds. Absent for a v0.1 worker's connection.

grid_snapshot_record.description: grid_snapshots bucket: session id → this record, one per session, the latest. The core's grid snapshot of a PTY shell session, so a restarted core (or a restarted VT worker) can restore the screen: the engine's own binary snapshot, opaque to the core, with the engine that produced it, the seq it is a snapshot of, and the grid's geometry. It carries no recording_offset: the session record's recording_committed_offset is the one copy (a second field meaning the same offset would be two counters that can drift). One persisted value: this record is written in the same bbolt write as the session record's commit point (recording_last_seq_out, recording_committed_offset), so at every write snapshot_seq equals recording_last_seq_out (C6 decision 2; 5.39: counters = one, aligned). A snapshot is forced on every PTY size change (applied size requests and the attach wiggle) and on alt-screen enter/exit/clear, so no resize ever lies between the last snapshot and a crash. If a snapshot cannot be taken (VT worker down) the commit point does not advance and the core raises an operator alert (alert.raised kind vt_unavailable). When a commit must land now (a realign, a gap's hold) and no snapshot comes within snapshot.wait_sec, or the VT worker cannot give one, the core deletes this record in the write of the session record that commits record-only (top); so does a snapshot it cannot restore (snapshot_incompatible), and the end of a session the core already knows. Until a new snapshot is stored the session commits record-only.

snapshot.description: Base64 of the engine's own binary snapshot, opaque to the core (unpadded input is padded; at least one byte). The engine name and version tell a reader whether a snapshot can be restored: a snapshot from another engine version is refused snapshot_incompatible.

snapshot_seq.description: The output seq the snapshot is of. It equals the session record's recording_last_seq_out in the same bbolt write — one counter, aligned (5.39) — and is what the C3 hello carries as last_committed_seq: the core realigns before every hello (top). A snapshot is stored only at or past the commit point, so the commit point never moves backwards.

cols.description: The grid's width when the snapshot was taken: the PTY's size at that moment.

name.description: The VT engine's name. A string, not a constant: libghostty-vt is the locked engine and vt10x is the fallback implementation, and a later tag may pin a different version.

version.description: The engine's version, as the pin records it. A snapshot from another version is refused snapshot_incompatible, and the stale flow is raised with cause grid_lost.

engine.description: Which VT engine produced the snapshot.

written_at.description: When the snapshot was persisted, in UTC with Z.
